facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is Lohuecotitan pandafilandi, which was described and named in 2016.
facts.quote: The only species known in the genus is Lohuecotitan pandafilandi, described and named in 2016.

facts.statement: The fossil-bearing formation dates from the Upper Campanian to the Lower Maastrichtian and represented a muddy coastal floodplain.
facts.quote: The formation dates from the Upper Campanian to the Lower Maastrichtian, and would have represented a muddy coastal floodplain.

facts.statement: The fossil locality was discovered in 2007 during the construction of the Madrid-Valencia high-speed railway.
facts.quote: The locality was discovered in 2007 during the cutting of a little hill for installation of the railway of the Madrid-Valencia high-speed train.

facts.statement: More than 10,000 fossils have been collected, including over twenty sets of partial titanosaur skeletons in anatomical connection.
facts.quote: More than 10 000 fossils have been collected, almost half of which belong to titanosaurs comprising more than twenty sets of partial skeletons in anatomical connection or with a low dispersion of their skeletal elements.

facts.statement: The genus name Lohuecotitan combines the type locality with the Greek word 'titan'.
facts.quote: The name of Lohuecotitan combines a reference to the type locality with titan (which refers to the Greek titans).

facts.statement: Lohuecotitan possesses unique characteristics not seen in other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Lohuecotitan was recognized by its describers as having a number of unique characteristics (autapomorphies) not seen in other titanosaurs.

facts.statement: The neural spine of the vertebra appears V-shaped from the side and resembles a Greek cross in cross-section.
facts.quote: In addition, due to the way that the prespinal and postspinal laminae project upwards, the neural spine of the vertebra appears to be V-shaped from the side, and resemble a Greek cross in cross-section.

facts.statement: The cervical and dorsal vertebrae are opisthocoelous, while the caudal vertebrae are procoelous.
facts.quote: The cervical and dorsal vertebrae are opisthocoelous; the caudal vertebrae were procoelous (a characteristic common in Lithostrotia).

facts.statement: The braincase MCCM-HUE-8741 is small, with a front-to-back length of 100.8 mm and a maximum left half width of 64.3 mm.
facts.quote: The braincase, MCCM-HUE-8741, is small in size overall, with a front-to-back length of 100.8 mm, and the maximum width of the left half being 64.3 mm.

facts.statement: The occipital condyle measures 28.6 mm in width and 15.8 mm in height.
facts.quote: The occipital condyle is 28.6 mm wide and 15.8 mm tall.

facts.statement: The semicircular canals are contracted and highly curved.
facts.quote: The semicircular canals are contracted, and they are highly curved.

facts.statement: Gorscak & O'Connor (2019) recovered Lohuecotitan as a saltasaurid.
facts.quote: In the same year, Gorscak & O'Connor (2019) in their description of Mnyamawamtuka recovered Lohuecotitan as a saltasaurid.

facts.statement: It lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 72 million years ago during the Maastrichtian, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: el cual vivió durante a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 millones de años durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Lohuecotitan was a relatively large sauropod measuring between 15 and 20 meters in length, though its neck length is unknown.
facts.quote: Lohuecotitan era un saurópodo relativamente grande, de entre 15 a 20 metros de longitud, dependiendo de la longitud del cuello la cual no es conocida.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Lohuecotitan possess only a short crest on the posterior side of their spinous processes.
facts.quote: Las vértebras solo tienen una corta cresta en la parte posterior de sus procesos espinosos.

facts.statement: The ilium of Lohuecotitan is pneumatized, meaning it is filled with internal air spaces.
facts.quote: El ilion se encuentra neumatizado, es decir lleno de espacios internos con aire.

facts.statement: The species Lohuecotitan pandafilandi was named and described in 2016 by Verónica Díez Díaz, Pedro Mocho, Adrián Páramo, Fernando Escaso, Fátima Marcos Fernández, José Luis Sanz, and Francisco Ortega.
facts.quote: En 2016, se nombró y describió a la especie tipo Lohuecotitan pandafilandi por Verónica Díez Díaz, Pedro Mocho, Adrián Páramo, Fernando Escaso, Fátima Marcos Fernández, José Luis Sanz y Francisco Ortega.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Lohuecotitan were discovered at the Lo Hueco site in Fuentes, Cuenca, Spain.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles fueron descubiertos en el yacimiento de Lo Hueco, de Fuentes, Cuenca, España.

facts.statement: The genus name Lohuecotitan references the fossil site name combined with the term 'titan,' alluding to the giants of Greek mythology.
facts.quote: El nombre del género hace referencia al nombre del sitio fósil junto con el término titan, aludiendo a aquellos gigantes de la mitología griega.

facts.statement: The species name pandafilandi refers to the giant Pandafilando de la Fosca Vista, a character from Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra's novel Don Quixote, commemorating the 400th anniversary of the author in 2016.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere al gigante Pandafilando de la Fosca Vista, personaje de la novela El ingenioso hidalgo Don Quijote de la Mancha, de Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra, de quien se conmemoraba su 400° aniversario en 2016.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including three cervical vertebrae, six dorsal vertebrae, parts of sacral vertebrae, twenty caudal vertebrae, ribs, chevrons, a left ulna, both ischia, a left pubis, part of the right foot, and some indeterminate bones.
facts.quote: Consiste de un esqueleto parcial sin el cráneo. Se encontraron tres vértebras cervicales, seis dorsales, partes de las vértebras del sacro, veinte vértebras caudales, costillas, cheurones, una ulna izquierda, ambos isquiones, un pubis izquierdo y una parte del pie derecho, además de algunos huesos indeterminados.

facts.statement: Descriptores placed Lohuecotitan within the clade Lithostrotia, noting it is more derived than Malawisaurus on the cladogram.
facts.quote: Lohuecotitan fue situado por sus descriptores dentro del clado Lithostrotia, siendo más derivado que Malawisaurus en el cladograma.

facts.statement: The exact relationship of Lohuecotitan to other derived lithostrotians such as Opisthocoelicaudia, Alamosaurus, Trigonosaurus, Saltasaurinae, and Nemegtosauridae could not be determined.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, no se pudo determinar su relación exacta con otros litostrotios igualmente derivados como Opisthocoelicaudia, Alamosaurus, Trigonosaurus, los Saltasaurinae y los Nemegtosauridae.

facts.statement: Lohuecotitan lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian time range, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Lohuecotitan is Eutitanosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eutitanosauria

facts.statement: Lohuecotitan belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Lohuecotitan confirms that a rich radiation of titanosaurs occurred in the late Cretaceous in Europe, specifically on the ancient Iberian-Armorican island.
facts.quote: Lohuecotitan confirma por su parte que se produjo una rica radiación de titanosaurios a finales del Cretácico en Europa, y más precisamente en la antigua isla íbero-armoricana.
